title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as funding flows into optical ground stations and lunar defense initiatives take shape. Meanwhile, acquisitions and partnerships signal a push towards more integrated and resilient space capabilities.

themes.title: Funding for Optical Solutions
themes.body: QOSMIC's recent $3.33 million raise highlights a growing interest in the orbital data economy. As optical ground stations become a focal point, expect more players to enter this niche market.

themes.title: Acquisitions and Partnerships
themes.body: Voyager's acquisition of Astrobotic and Anduril's collaboration with L3Harris underscore a trend towards consolidation in the space industry. These moves are likely aimed at enhancing technological capabilities and market positioning.

themes.title: Defense Budget Increases
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience reflects a strategic pivot towards bolstering national security in space. This infusion of funds could lead to accelerated development and deployment of critical technologies.

themes.title: Challenges in Hypersonics
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing point to persistent technical hurdles in this high-stakes arena. As the third quarter slips by without progress, the implications for defense strategies remain uncertain.
